findings.remediation: Remove install-time side effects or document and review each lifecycle script.
findings.impact: Install-time lifecycle scripts run before the package is reviewed at runtime and inherit installer privileges.
findings.attack_vector: package.json declares preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare code that npm may execute during installation.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: decodes obfuscated payload and executes it in the same file
findings.remediation: Remove all decode-and-execute patterns; they are strongly correlated with malicious behavior.
findings.impact: Decoded payload executed in same file — classic obfuscation-to-RCE pattern.
findings.attack_vector: Buffer.from(base64).toString() → eval() chain; the base64 payload is invisible to static review.

findings.message: uses eval() or new Function() to execute dynamically generated code
findings.remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and use fixed allowlisted implementations.
findings.impact: Dynamic eval/Function executes code that is difficult to audit and becomes code injection if external input reaches it.
findings.attack_vector: Source uses eval()/new Function(); this rule alone does not prove that an attacker controls the evaluated value.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: constructs a regular expression from a non-literal value (possible ReDoS)
findings.basis: OWASP Regular Expression Denial of Service Prevention
findings.remediation: Use bounded, allowlisted patterns and enforce input and execution limits for dynamic regular expressions.
findings.impact: An attacker-controlled regular expression can consume excessive CPU and deny service.
findings.attack_vector: A non-literal value is passed to RegExp without pattern or execution bounds.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
